title: Israel Rejects Trump's 15-Point Plan for Gaza, Says Netanyahu
subtitle: Prime Minister States Israeli Forces Will Only Leave When Hamas is Fully Disarmed
excerpt: Israel rejects Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza, Netanyahu says troops won't leave until Hamas is disarmed.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Israel's government has announced that it will not accept the 15-point plan proposed by Trump for the Gaza region. The decision was made by the Prime Minister, who highlighted that the proposal does not meet the criteria established by Tel Aviv.

Condition for Troop Withdrawal

According to the Prime Minister, Israeli military forces will remain in Gaza until the Hamas group is genuinely disarmed. The demand for the total disarmament of Hamas has been reiterated as an indispensable condition for any withdrawal movement.

This stance reflects the common practice of governments evaluating external proposals in light of their own security objectives. When an external plan is presented, the recipient government usually analyzes whether it meets the fundamental demands of its defense policy before considering its implementation.

In Israel's case, the evaluation of Trump's plan is linked to control over the military capacity of armed groups in the region. The requirement that Hamas be truly disarmed indicates that the country's security strategy remains focused on neutralizing threats before advancing with changes in troop positioning.

Thus, the rejection of the 15-point plan and the maintenance of a military presence in Gaza are presented as decisions aligned with the objective of ensuring that any withdrawal occurs only under security conditions considered satisfactory by Israeli authorities.

With information from BBC News.
